observations: Photo 0 shows a car engine bay/engine assembly on a stand or floor, with visible intake/exhaust piping, fuel/ignition components, and multiple sensors/solenoids.
Photo 0 includes a visible alternator-like unit and a belt-driven pulley at the lower right area.
Photo 1 shows the same engine from a different angle; belt/pulleys are visible including a large crank/drive pulley area and an alternator at the left.
No clear engine ID plate, engine code, VIN tag, or brand/model marking is readable in either photo.

claims.evidence: Neither photo shows a readable engine code/plate or clear Hyundai/Kia branding to confirm make/model; only a generic 4-cylinder engine assembly is visible.

risks.risk: Exact engine make/model (Hyundai vs Kia vs other) and engine code are not readable, so compatibility and correct parts matching are uncertain.
risks.proof: A clear close-up photo of the engine identification plate/engine code stamping (or the full engine code on the block/head) plus the gearbox bellhousing mating area.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as the worst-case generic 4-cylinder engine with unknown code/compatibility risk (assume may not match buyer’s car without extra parts).

risks.risk: Unknown running condition (may be seized, missing parts, or have internal faults). Photos only show components, not operation.
risks.proof: Video of the engine cranking/running (even short start) with oil pressure/temperature behavior visible, or a compression test report.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as not proven working (worst case: treat as for parts/needs overhaul).

risks.risk: Missing accessories/ancillaries or incomplete harness (photos may not show everything included).
risks.proof: A photo checklist laid out: alternator, starter, AC compressor, power steering pump, injectors, coils, sensors, ECU, wiring harness, and all hoses—showing what is included.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as incomplete/unknown inclusion (worst case: buyer may need to source missing items).

risks.risk: Cooling/oil system leaks or damaged components (cracks, bent pipes, worn pulleys/belts) cannot be confirmed from these angles.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of: cylinder head surface, oil pan area, timing cover area, and any wet/damaged spots; plus a leak test or pressure test result.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as may require reseal/repairs (worst case: assume leaks/maintenance needed).

proof_requests: Clear close-up of the engine code/ID plate on the block/head (readable characters).
Video of the engine cranking and ideally starting/running (showing it turns over strongly).
List of included items (ECU, harness, starter, alternator, injectors, coils, sensors, turbo/AC/PS if applicable) with photos of each.
Compression test or leak test report (or at least a mechanic’s test sheet).
response.reason: The photos show a 4-cylinder engine assembly but do not provide readable engine identification or proof of working condition. Without engine code and run/test evidence, the correct pricing cannot be safely determined.
